challenge.description: Deliver at least 10 MW average grid electricity at year 10, using the least mined Mercury ore. Fixed seed, imported-tech reserve, efficiencies and transmission hardware.

warnings: Illustrative engineering scenario; no forecast of construction cost or readiness.
Circular display orbits are schematic. Collisions, eccentricity, station keeping and launch trajectories are not integrated.
Seed plant, imported technology reserve and Earth relay infrastructure are starting endowments; their delivery and capital cost are excluded.
Imported precision components are exhausted; industrial self-replication is not assumed.
Ground beam intensity or instantaneous grid capacity curtails transmission.

proposal.title: Seed-Powered, Zero-Expansion Optical Mission
proposal.rationale: Move inward to 0.3 AU and set the radiator ratio just above the 600 K thermal boundary, maximizing collector power per manufactured kilogram. Keep the optical relay because direct microwave transmission is highly lossy and space-only supplies no grid electricity. Set factory expansion and electricity reinvestment to zero: the fixed seed plant alone sustains limited production, all manufactured hardware becomes collectors, and no power is diverted from the grid. This should sharply reduce ore consumption versus the import-limited baseline while retaining substantial delivery margin. Uncertainty is concentrated in monthly energy-limited throughput and activation timing; the small radiator margin also depends on numerical treatment near the thermal cutoff.

proposal.title: Thermal-Edge Optical Mission
proposal.rationale: Retain the proven zero-expansion, zero-reinvestment architecture and optical relay. Set 0.3 AU for maximum incident flux, while lowering radiator ratio from 1.46 to approximately 1.4527, just above the analytical 600 K boundary. This slightly improves generated power per manufactured kilogram without increasing industrial demand, so the seed-powered, energy-limited production path remains the least-mining strategy available through these controls. A small thermal margin is retained for floating-point evaluation. Uncertainty is dominated by monthly activation and retirement timing; because the previous design already reached the link ceiling, the improvement may preserve feasibility rather than materially reduce ore.

proposal.title: Minimum-Ore Thermal-Edge Optical Mission
proposal.rationale: Use the proven minimum-production architecture: one seed-powered factory, no expansion, no orbital-power reinvestment, and the optical relay. Place collectors at 0.3 AU and set radiator ratio to 1.4526, marginally above the analytical 600 K boundary, maximizing delivered electricity per manufactured kilogram. Under the fixed just-in-time engine, seed-powered production continues throughout the mission, so the allowed policy fields provide no way to mine less than the demonstrated energy-limited quantity without disabling production; this proposal therefore targets the same apparent ore floor while maintaining more than 10 MW. Uncertainty is the extremely narrow thermal margin and floating-point treatment at the cutoff.
